haiku-low.q1: MySQL commits first, with an outbox row, in one transaction. Then one inline Postgres attempt (300 ms). A Postgres failure is ignored; the caller still succeeds, and the outbox row stays.
haiku-low.q2: Only when the stored version is lower than the incoming version. Equal versions are never replaced, and ids with a tombstone are skipped.
haiku-low.q3: Every instance reports dual, dual-write success is at least 99%, the oldest outbox row is under 60 s, the baseline is saved, and the replica has applied it. Instances can disagree on flags for up to 30 s.
haiku-low.q4: One process at a time, under a Postgres advisory lock. It pauses while replica lag exceeds 5 s or is missing, and reads at most 2,000 rows per batch.
haiku-low.q5: Reads: a zero-mismatch comparison pass within 24 h, then a ramp of 1, 10, 50, 100% with each level held an hour. Source of truth: 3 days at 100% reads, then a pre-switch checklist passes.
haiku-low.q6: An outbox row in the source database, written in the same transaction as the write. The drainer reads the current source row and applies it to the mirror, retrying forever until success.
haiku-low.q7: Tombstones in users_erased block re-creation: apply skips tombstoned ids. Erasure writes the mirror tombstone and deletes in one transaction, and backfill skips pending outbox ids. A rare gap is closed by the drainer.
haiku-low.q8: Progress is the cursor in migration_state.backfill_cursor, moved in the same Postgres transaction as its batch. It stops when a batch comes back empty, about 19,000 batches.
haiku-low.q9: The nightly and full comparison passes, using per-chunk checksums and primary re-checks. Persistent missing, extra, differing or erased-but-present rows go to the outbox. A higher Postgres version alerts and is not auto-fixed.
haiku-low.q10: The authority row: MySQL holder is set to switching under an exclusive lock, so writers get 503 and no instance writes MySQL-first. If the 20 s drain cap passes, holder reverts to mysql and the switch is investigated.
haiku-low.q11: Postgres assigns ids through its identity column. During each switch pause, setval sets it to GREATEST(MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT, max pg id) + 1000. On rollback, InnoDB's AUTO_INCREMENT moves past explicit ids.
haiku-low.q12: The reverse drainer copies Postgres outbox writes into MySQL for 14 days, with nightly comparisons. Rollback drains the outbox, switches the holder to mysql, and flips to dual, within 90 s. It ends when write_mode=pg revokes MySQL grants.

sonnet.q1: MySQL (source) is written first in one transaction (write plus outbox row); after commit, one inline attempt applies the row to Postgres (300 ms timeout). If Postgres fails, the error is ignored: the caller sees success, the outbox row stays, and a circuit breaker skips inline attempts for 10 s.
sonnet.q2: Only if the id has no tombstone and the stored version is lower than the incoming version (ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE ... WHERE users.version < EXCLUDED.version). Equal versions are never replaced; a row is inserted in full if absent.
sonnet.q3: Every instance must be confirmed dual-writing: instances reporting dual equals instances running, dual-write success rate at least 99%, oldest outbox row under 60 s, baseline gtid saved, and replica has applied the baseline with lag at most 5 s. Instances can disagree on flags for up to 30 s (flag refresh).
sonnet.q4: Only one backfill process runs (Postgres advisory lock). It pauses before each batch while mysql_replica_lag_seconds is above 5 or missing, reads from the replica (not primary) in batches of at most 2,000 rows by id order, with only a primary re-check per batch.
sonnet.q5: Reads: a zero-mismatch full comparison pass finished within the last 24 h (backfill finished, outbox empty); then ramp 1/10/50/100% holding each at least an hour, advancing only if fallback rate under 0.1%, latency acceptable, outbox age under 30 s, nightly comparison clean. Source of truth switch: 3+ days soak at 100% reads, new zero-mismatch full pass, outbox empty, reverse drainer deployed and idle, rollback rehearsed, switch scheduled in a low-traffic window (plus step 0 staging rehearsal).
sonnet.q6: The outbox row (users_sync_outbox: seq, user_id, enqueued_at), written in the same source-database (MySQL) transaction as the write, so it survives a crash. The drainer reads the current row from the source primary and applies it to Postgres (or applies a delete if gone), retrying forever with backoff and deleting the outbox row only on success.
sonnet.q7: Tombstones in users_erased (never removed, ids never reused); the apply rule skips any id with a tombstone. Deletes write the tombstone to the mirror first (best effort), and mirror delete and tombstone happen in one transaction. Backfill re-reads batches from the primary and skips missing ids or ids with pending outbox rows. A residual gap (both mirror steps failing plus a backfill batch landing in between) is closed by the drainer within seconds and covered by the outbox alert.
sonnet.q8: In Postgres table migration_state (backfill_cursor). The cursor is moved to the batch's last id in the same Postgres transaction that applies the batch. It stops when a batch comes back empty (about 19,000 batches); after a crash it resumes from the cursor and redoes any half-done batch harmlessly.
sonnet.q9: The full comparison pass (step 6, and nightly passes): per-chunk checksums by id range over (id, email, name, plan, version, updated_at) from the replica and Postgres; differing chunks are diffed row by row and re-checked against the primary after the outbox drains. Persistent mismatches (missing, extra, differing rows, erased ids still in MySQL) are each sent to the outbox for repair. A Postgres row with higher version than MySQL is a bug: alert, no auto-fix.
sonnet.q10: The authority row decides, not the flags: every write transaction reads users_authority with FOR SHARE and aborts with a retryable 503 (Retry-After) if holder isn't the expected database. The switch sets MySQL holder to switching (exclusive lock waits for in-flight writes, blocks new ones), drains the outbox, sets holders to pg, then flips the flag; stragglers not on dual_pg at T0+60 s are removed from the load balancer. If drain exceeds the 20 s cap, the MySQL holder is set back to mysql, ending the pause, and the operator investigates and retries; the pause is always under 90 s (expected 40-55 s).
sonnet.q11: Postgres assigns them (users.id BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY; copies carry explicit ids). During each switch pause (writes fenced, outbox drained) run setval(seq, GREATEST(MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT, max(pg id)) + 1000). On rollback, MySQL accepts explicit ids and InnoDB moves its AUTO_INCREMENT past them; a later second switch repeats the setval.
sonnet.q12: Every Postgres write has a durable Postgres outbox row, and the reverse drainer (plus inline apply) keeps MySQL current. Rollback (pause up to 90 s): set Postgres holder to switching, drain the Postgres outbox into MySQL until empty, set MySQL holder to mysql, flip flag to dual, wait until every instance reports dual. The option ends in step 12, at least 14 days after switched_at with a clean comparison: write_mode=pg, reverse drainer stopped, MySQL write grants revoked; after that lossless rollback is gone by design (flag back to dual_pg is safe only before grants are revoked).
